ancestries.name: Android
ancestries.description: Humanlike machines with a living spirit inside, built to serve and often slow to trust anyone who gives orders. They shrug off hazards like heat, cold, and poison, and take on each new Experience with real conviction.

features.name: With Purpose
features.rules: New Experiences start at +3 instead of +2.
features.short: New Experiences start at +3 instead of +2.

features.name: Constructed
features.rules: You have advantage to resist natural effects like heat, cold, disease, poison, and radiation.
features.short: Advantage to resist natural effects (heat, cold, disease, poison, radiation).

ancestries.name: Baruthu
ancestries.description: Glassy, drifting beings of Bretheda's skies who rework their own bodies as the situation demands. They hover rather than walk, and can loosen their form to soften a hard hit.

features.name: Reconfigure
features.rules: When you would take Major or greater damage, you may mark a Stress to reduce the damage threshold by 1.
features.short: When you would take Major or greater damage, mark a Stress to reduce that threshold by 1.

features.name: Floating
features.rules: You can fly. Mark a Stress to propel yourself a far distance without needing the standard Agility Trait roll.
features.short: You can fly. Mark a Stress to move a far distance with no Agility roll.

ancestries.name: Kasatha
ancestries.description: Tall, long-limbed people with four arms, from a tradition that prizes order, courtesy, and obligation. Allies lean on their reliability, and the spare pair of arms holds an extra off-hand weapon.

features.name: Reliable
features.rules: When you assist an ally by spending a Hope, you gain a Hope if they succeed.
features.short: When you spend a Hope to assist an ally, gain a Hope if they succeed.

features.name: Four-armed
features.rules: You can wield an additional secondary weapon. Gain the benefits of all secondary weapons. Passive and reactive benefits stack where reasonable.
features.short: Wield an extra secondary weapon and gain the benefits of all of them; passive and reactive benefits stack where reasonable.

ancestries.name: Lashunta
ancestries.description: A mind-touched people from Castrovel's city-states who speak thought to thought through the antennae on their brows. They can open a link between allies, or pry loose an unwilling target's fears and secrets.

features.name: Limited Telepathy
features.rules: Spend a Hope to allow willing targets in Far range of you to communicate with you and each other through your mind. You hear all of this conversation. This effect ends for each target as they leave Far range or take a long rest.
features.short: Spend a Hope: willing targets in Far range speak mind to mind with you and each other, and you hear it all. Ends for a target when it leaves Far range or takes a long rest.

features.name: Open Minded
features.rules: Once per rest, you can extend your telepathic abilities to an unwilling target in Far range. Mark a Stress to roll a number of d6s equal to your Presence or Instinct trait. If you roll any 4s, learn what they fear now. Any 5s: what they will do next. Any 6s: what they wish to keep secret.
features.short: Once per rest, mark a Stress and roll d6s equal to your Presence or Instinct against an unwilling target in Far range. Any 4: what it fears now. Any 5: what it will do next. Any 6: what it wishes to keep secret.

ancestries.name: Pahtra
ancestries.description: Tall, furred, cat-like people who treasure personal freedom, music, and combat, and who prove themselves in the wild as youths. Their reflexes are sharp, and their claws pay off when a strike lands with Hope.

features.name: Nimble
features.rules: You have advantage on Agility, Finesse, and Instinct reaction rolls.
features.short: Advantage on Agility, Finesse, and Instinct reaction rolls.

features.name: Retractable Claws
features.rules: Your claws are an Agility or Finesse Melee weapon dealing d6 physical damage using your Proficiency. Once per rest, when an attack using your claws succeeds with Hope, gain an additional Hope.
features.short: Claws: Agility or Finesse, Melee, d6 physical using your Proficiency. Once per rest, when a claw attack succeeds with Hope, gain an additional Hope.

ancestries.name: Shirren
ancestries.description: Insect-like people with hard shells and feelered heads, once bound to the Swarm's hive mind and now independent yet team-minded. They speak mind to mind with anyone nearby and lift friends who falter.

features.name: Universal Telepathy
features.rules: Spend a Hope to communicate with a target in Close range. They can understand you, though they are not compelled to respond. You can understand them regardless of language or sapience barrier.
features.short: Spend a Hope to communicate with a target in Close range; they understand you but need not respond. You understand them regardless of language or sapience.

features.name: Encouraging Vibes
features.rules: When a target in Close range fails an action roll, you can mark a Stress to allow them to reroll either die.
features.short: When a target in Close range fails an action roll, mark a Stress to let them reroll either die.

ancestries.name: Skittermander
ancestries.description: Small, fuzzy, many-armed helpers around three feet tall with a sunny outlook. They are tough to pin down, and will climb a much larger foe and cling on to hinder it.

features.name: Hug Master
features.rules: As an action, you can make an Agility roll against a target larger than yourself to climb it. On a success, they temporarily gain the Hugged condition. While Hugged: they cannot attack you, but can force an Agility Reaction roll from you to free themselves; you move with them; attacks against you that miss hit them; mark a Stress as a reaction to impose disadvantage on actions they take. Hugged ends when you leave melee range, you fail the reaction roll above, or the GM spends a Fear to end it.
features.short: Agility roll against a larger target to climb it; on a success it is Hugged. Hugged: it cannot attack you but can force an Agility Reaction roll from you to break free; you move with it; attacks against you that miss hit it; mark a Stress to impose disadvantage on its actions. Ends if you leave melee range, fail that reaction roll, or the GM spends a Fear.

features.name: Tiny Chaotic Target
features.rules: Gain a +1 to your Evasion.
features.short: +1 Evasion.

ancestries.name: Vesk
ancestries.description: Hulking, scaly warriors from a society that ranks people by martial skill. They sniff out hidden quarry, gain Hope through combat, and make attackers who miss pay.

features.name: Blood Sense
features.rules: Spend a Hope to hone in on biological scents nearby. Biological or partially biological creatures in Far range from you cannot hide from you and you have advantage on action rolls to follow their trail.
features.short: Spend a Hope: biological or partly biological creatures in Far range cannot hide from you, and you have advantage to track them.

features.name: Cradled by War
features.rules: When your attack against an adversary succeeds, mark a Stress to gain a Hope. When an attack against you fails, spend a Hope to force your attacker to mark a Hit Point.
features.short: When your attack succeeds, mark a Stress to gain a Hope. When an attack against you fails, spend a Hope to make the attacker mark a Hit Point.

ancestries.name: Ysoki
ancestries.description: Small, ratlike people who dwell in crowded warrens or roaming caravans and love to tinker. They are slippery in a scramble and bite hard, through gear and foes alike.

features.name: Scurry
features.rules: When you move further than Very Close range, gain the Scurrying condition. Lose Scurrying at the start of your next Spotlight. While Scurrying, you have +2 Evasion.
features.short: When you move further than Very Close range, you are Scurrying until the start of your next Spotlight: +2 Evasion.

features.name: Bite-Sized
features.rules: You have sharp teeth that are a Strength or Finesse Melee weapon dealing d4+2 using your Proficiency. You can mark a Stress to chew through thin metal, plastic, fibers, etc. Depending on thickness this may require an action roll. If you successfully damage an adversary with a bite, mark a Stress to give them the Chewed condition, which lowers their thresholds by 3 each.
features.short: Bite: Strength or Finesse, Melee, d4+2 using your Proficiency. Mark a Stress to chew through thin metal, plastic, or fibers (thick material may need an action roll). After a bite damages an adversary, mark a Stress to give it Chewed: its thresholds drop by 3 each.

communities.name: Hubborne
communities.description: Absalom Station: Floating in Lost Golarion's empty orbit, this bustling space station is the center of interstellar trade and governance among the Pact Worlds. The people who live here are accustomed to the hustle and bustle and are always looking for their next opportunity.

features.name: Well Connected
features.rules: At the start of a rest, refuel, or refit, gain tokens equal to the number of players at the table. At the end of the rest, refuel, or refit, distribute the tokens as you like among yourself and any other players. Each token clears an Armor Slot, a Stress, or a Hit Point, or grants a Hope.
features.short: At the start of a rest, refuel, or refit, gain tokens equal to the number of players. At its end, hand them out as you like to yourself and others. Each token clears an Armor Slot, a Stress, or a Hit Point, or grants a Hope.

communities.name: Spikeborn
communities.description: Absalom Station: The Spike is the cramped, lawless underside of the station, beneath the wealthy Eye and next to the reactor. Its children learn the hidden passages, who sells favors, and which debts to avoid.

features.name: One Eye Open
features.rules: Once per scene, while you are Hidden, you may mark a Stress to gain a Hope.
features.short: Once per scene, while Hidden, mark a Stress to gain a Hope.

communities.name: Scrapborn
communities.description: Akiton: Akiton's dry wastes are littered with wrecked ships, played-out mines, and feuding cities. Its people live off salvage and oddities pulled from the wreckage, and believe only what they have tried themselves.

features.name: Upcycling
features.rules: In each new scene that contains scraps, garbage, or fallen adversaries, you may add 1 to your Junk Count, which has no upper limit. During a rest, spend Junk on your junk roll: Junk spent as dice adds that many dice to the roll, and Junk spent as a bonus adds that bonus to each die. Roll the junk dice, add the bonus to each, and pick your favorite result from the consumable table.
features.short: In each new scene with scraps, garbage, or fallen adversaries, you may add 1 to your Junk Count (no upper limit). During a rest, spend Junk on your junk roll: each spent as a die adds a die, each spent as a bonus adds +1 to every die. Pick your favorite result from the consumable table.

communities.name: Townbound
communities.description: Akiton: Many on Akiton live in settlements owned by a single company that supplies the home, the shop, and the paycheck. They know long shifts, mounting debt, and the quiet ways workers cover for each other.

features.name: I've Got Your Back
features.rules: Once per rest, you can encourage an ally with kind words or action. You gain a Hope and they clear up to 3 Stress.
features.short: Once per rest, encourage an ally with words or action: you gain a Hope and they clear up to 3 Stress.

communities.name: Asanan
communities.description: Castrovel: In the lashunta cities of Asana, universities and businesses share the same busy streets, and a major spaceport links them to the system. Locals treat learning as a form of wealth and skill as a vocation.

features.name: Asanan Learner
features.rules: Gain an Experience, Asanan Learner, whose bonus is set to your highest Experience bonus each long rest. It applies only to non-violent action rolls. Each use reduces its bonus by 1.
features.short: Gain an Experience, Asanan Learner, whose bonus is set to your highest Experience bonus each long rest. It applies only to non-violent action rolls. Each use reduce by 1.

communities.name: Wardenborn
communities.description: Castrovel: Castrovel's wild preserves are lovely and dangerous, and the Xenowardens guard them. Those raised in their care learn to defend wildlife and to give it its due respect.

features.name: Wildsense
features.rules: You know the ways of non-sapient creatures. When one attacks you, you have +2 Evasion against that attack. When you attack one, you can make it mark Stress instead of Hit Points, one for one. On a successful Presence Action Roll, you can make all Vulnerable ones within Close range flee.
features.short: Against non-sapient creatures: +2 Evasion when they attack you; when you attack one, it can mark Stress instead of Hit Points, one for one. On a successful Presence Action Roll, all Vulnerable ones within Close range flee.

communities.name: Hivebound
communities.description: Castrovel: The formian Colonies are cooperating hives devoted to the Overqueen and built around making things. Their people prize teamwork, defined duties, and tasks done right.

features.name: Duty Bound
features.rules: At each rest, state your new duty in one sentence. When you act under this duty, you can spend a Hope to gain +2 to the action roll. If it succeeds, gain a Hope.
features.short: At each rest, state a new duty in one sentence. When you act under it, spend a Hope for +2 to the action roll. On a success, gain a Hope.

communities.name: Ringborn
communities.description: Verces: Verces has a blazing side and a frozen side, and its population crowds into the thin habitable band between, shared by 27 nations. Natives are skilled with machines and implants, and used to debating over borders.

features.name: Negotiator
features.rules: You have advantage on rolls to reach a compromise when you are willing to give something up. If no compromise is reached, you can spend a Hope to make the GM lose a Fear.
features.short: Advantage on rolls to reach a compromise when you are willing to give something up. If none is reached, spend a Hope to make the GM lose a Fear.

communities.name: Fringeborn
communities.description: Verces: Beyond the Ring lie the Outlaw Kingdoms, a refuge for exiles, fugitives, cultists, and survivors of the desert and the ice. Those raised there follow their own codes and expect nothing from the Ring's authorities.

features.name: Rulebreaker
features.rules: With a moment of observation, you sense who is in charge and what they generally want. You can also sense tension in the ranks, if it exists. Spend a Hope and have a moment of conversation to gain a small favor if you act on this knowledge.
features.short: After a moment of observation, you sense who is in charge, what they generally want, and any tension in the ranks. Spend a Hope and a moment of conversation to gain a small favor if you act on this.

communities.name: Legionborn
communities.description: Triaxus: Triaxus endures long, harsh winters, and the Skyfire Legion is the mercenary host that guards its lands and sells its swords across the system. Those who grew up in its shadow can hold a line and read a contract.

features.name: Front Line
features.rules: You may make a Reaction Roll appropriate to the situation to stop an adversary's movement when it is within Very Close range, or to force it to target you instead of something behind you.
features.short: Make a fitting Reaction Roll to stop an adversary within Very Close range from moving, or to force it to target you instead of something behind you.

communities.name: Cloudborn
communities.description: Bretheda: Bretheda's people dwell in floating cities high in a gas giant's air, under the barathu Confluence. They watch the winds, scan the sky, and keep steady when the weather turns.

features.name: Weather Vein
features.rules: Once per spotlight, spend a Hope to clear a mental condition from yourself or from an ally within Very Close range.
features.short: Once per spotlight, spend a Hope to clear a mental condition from yourself or an ally within Very Close range.

communities.name: Moonbound
communities.description: Bretheda: The moons around Bretheda include industrial water worlds, crystal caverns, and gem mines worked by bonded and convicted labor. Those raised there learn risky work, tough deals, and who is quietly buying their way out.

features.name: Worker's Bond
features.rules: You have advantage on rolls to speak with working-class or lower-class people about what is really going on, and to examine a work site for abnormalities, exits, and opportunities.
features.short: Advantage on rolls to learn from working-class or lower-class people what is really going on, and to examine a work site for abnormalities, exits, and opportunities.

communities.name: Roselit
communities.description: Liavara: Roselight is a floating platform-city that mines gas from Liavara, where quotas and barathu firms set the pace. Its people tend floating gardens and know how to keep a sealed living system going.

features.name: Self Contained
features.rules: At the start of each session, gain Rose tokens equal to your level. Spend a Rose token to: (A) clear a Stress, once per spotlight; (B) clear an Armor Slot or a Hit Point, up to twice per rest; or (C) give yourself and one ally within Close range 1 Hope each, once per session.
features.short: Each session, gain Rose tokens equal to your level. Spend one to: (A) clear a Stress, once per spotlight; (B) clear an Armor Slot or Hit Point, twice per rest; (C) give yourself and one ally within Close range 1 Hope each, once per session.

communities.name: Domeborn
communities.description: Apostae: Apostae has almost no air, so elven noble houses rule from enchanted domes while competing weapons makers drive the economy. Natives understand arms, corporate rivalry, and when to leave a question unasked.

features.name: Weapon Specialist
features.rules: You can switch weapons without marking a Stress. When you attack with a tech weapon, you can mark a Stress to reroll all damage dice.
features.short: Switch weapons without marking a Stress. When you attack with a tech weapon, mark a Stress to reroll all damage dice.

communities.name: Beltborn
communities.description: The Diaspora: The Diaspora is a scatter of asteroids and wreckage inhabited by dwarf miners, android refugees, monks, and Free Captain pirates. Its people are self-reliant, inventive, and used to scraping by with little law.

features.name: Wary
features.rules: When the first attack of a scene is made, you can make an attack as a Reaction Roll. On a success, gain a Hope. You have advantage on rolls to spot lies and hidden things.
features.short: When the first attack of a scene is made, you can make an attack as a Reaction Roll; on a success, gain a Hope. Advantage on rolls to spot lies and hidden things.

classes.name: Envoy
classes.classItems: A diplomatic seal worn smooth from years of handling or a tin of tea from a world that no longer has a name

hopeFeature.name: Envoy Hope Feature
hopeFeature.rules: Spend any number of Hope to warn and/or encourage an ally. They increase their Evasion or next action roll by 2 plus the Hope you spent until the end of their next spotlight or your next spotlight.

features.name: Squad Goals
features.rules: When you move to a point in Close range, mark a Stress to bring up to two willing creatures in Very Close range of your starting point with you. When you attack an adversary, mark a Stress to allow an ally in Very Close range of you to make an attack against the same adversary as a reaction.

features.name: Tactical Mind
features.rules: You have Envoy Tokens, up to a maximum of 6. When you would gain Hope, you may gain an Envoy Token instead. When you long rest, gain Envoy Tokens equal to your Spellcast Trait. You can spend an Envoy Token instead of Hope to aid an ally.

backgroundQuestions: Which station, academy, or ship taught you that a promise is the strongest tool you own, and who broke one to you?
Who was the first person you ever talked out of a fight, and what did it cost you with the people on the other side?
Who gave you your first posting, and what did they leave out when they described it?
connections: I spoke up for you when you were the newest face in the room. Who were we facing, and how did you thank me afterward?
I once brought you to a meal where the food, the seating, or the toasts meant something. Where were we, and what did you learn?
I taught you a phrase in a language from my home. What does it mean, and when did you first use it?

classes.name: Mystic
classes.classItems: A prism that hums softly when no one is near or a letter in a script you have never managed to read

hopeFeature.name: Mystic Hope Feature
hopeFeature.rules: Spend 3 Hope to reroll a Spellcast Roll.

features.name: Mystic Bond
features.rules: Each rest you can designate up to 10 creatures to be part of your Mystic Bond. At each of your spotlights, you may mark a Stress to let one of them clear a Stress.

features.name: Vitality Network
features.rules: You have a pool of Vitality Points (VP). After a long rest, refill it to its maximum of your Spellcast Trait + your Tier. Once per spotlight, you may spend 2 VP to allow someone within your Mystic Bond to clear a Stress or a Hit Point.

backgroundQuestions: Where were you the first time you heard the signal in the dark between stars, and why didn't you tell anyone?
Which place did you leave behind because it had started to feel like it was listening to you?
Who taught you to quiet your mind, and why did you stop practicing with them?
connections: I sat up with you through a bad night. What did I say to keep you steady?
I once followed a strange pull toward a place and you came along. What was waiting there?
What small, ordinary thing do you do that steadies me when my gifts feel too loud?

classes.name: Operative
classes.classItems: A coin with a hidden seam that has never opened or a single key that fits no lock you have found yet

hopeFeature.name: Operative Hope Feature
hopeFeature.rules: Spend 2 Hope when you make an action roll to add an Experience and gain advantage on the roll.

features.name: Tech Savvy
features.rules: Gain an additional domain card at level 1. On all domain cards, replace the words "Spell" and "Magic" with "Tech", and "Grimoire" with "Kit". If you swap out a Tech or Kit card, reduce the Stress cost to do so by 1.

features.name: Called Shot
features.rules: If you have not moved during your spotlight, you can make a Called Shot. Make an attack roll with a weapon of range Close or farther. On a hit, mark a Stress to deal an extra Pd4 damage. Your spotlight ends after the shot.

backgroundQuestions: Which crew, agency, or syndicate gave you your first real job, and what did they call you?
You spent a season living under a false name on a world you came to like. Where was it, and who still wonders where you went?
What small job did you take for the money that you wish you had turned down?
connections: I once covered for you when your story started to fall apart. Where were we, and what did it cost me?
I once told you my real name: __________. What did you do that made me think you earned it?
I gave you a signal that means it is safe to come in. What is it, and when did you first use it?

classes.name: Solarian
classes.classItems: A shard of a dead star sealed in glass or a scorched pilgrim's ribbon you were given and never returned

hopeFeature.name: Solarian Hope Feature
hopeFeature.rules: Spend 3 Hope to summon all 3 Solar Conjurations.

features.name: Twin Energies
features.rules:
You have two modes, Graviton and Photon, between which you can switch at the start of your spotlight. When you switch, you may perform a Solar Conjuration of a Mote, Weapon, or Aura. Your conjurations take on your mode with each switch.
- Solar Mote: Create a floating mote of energy that orbits you. You may choose to fire it at an adversary when you make a ranged attack roll for an additional +1d6 damage.
- Solar Weapon: Create a melee weapon that deals d8 Tech damage and uses your Spellcast Trait. Then choose one: Very Close range, d10+2 damage, or the feature "Reliable: +1 to attack rolls." Add your Tier and Spellcast Trait to your damage.
- Solar Aura: Create a cloud of energy churning around you. When you take damage, you can destroy your Aura to reduce the damage by one threshold.

backgroundQuestions: What star or great light did you first feel pulling at you, and who was beside you when it did?
Which order, school, or stubborn mentor taught you the first steps of holding a star's power, and what did they forbid?
You once lost your temper and something you cared about got scorched. What was it?
connections: I had a very bad day and you were there for it. What happened, and what did I ask you to keep to yourself?
I promised to show you the place where my star was born. What are you hoping we find there?
What do you do when my light flickers that lets me know you are there?

classes.name: Soldier
classes.classItems: A dented service plate with names scratched into the back or a half-finished letter to someone you cannot reach

hopeFeature.name: Soldier Hope Feature
hopeFeature.rules: While you have more than 4 Hope, you can spend a Hope instead of marking an Armor Slot.

features.name: Suppression
features.rules: When you make a weapon attack, spend a Hope to make your target temporarily Suppressed. While Suppressed, their action rolls have disadvantage, and if they move from their position their spotlight ends. Their Suppressed condition ends when they move or voluntarily mark a Stress.

features.name: Dread Abilities
features.rules: All Dread domain card spells are now abilities instead. Dread spells that target a creature deal no damage. Instead, when you succeed on a weapon attack you can apply the non-damaging effects of the Dread spell to the target in place of the Suppressed condition. Dread spells that do not target a creature work as written but count as abilities. Use Strength for any Spellcast Roll or Spellcast Trait a Dread card calls for. Describe Dread effects as fear, suppression, and pressure, not necromancy.

backgroundQuestions: Which garrison, academy, or mercenary company trained you, and who from it still sends you word?
You were left holding a post after everyone else had been called away. What were you guarding, and who found out you stayed?
What rule from your old unit do you still follow, even when no one is watching?
connections: I helped you through your first real fight. Where were we, and what did we say afterward?
I once followed an order I still wonder about, and I told you what it was. What was it, and what did you say?
We shared a watch on a long, quiet night. What did I tell you about home that I have told no one else?

classes.name: Witchwarper
classes.classItems: A clock that always runs at the wrong speed or a photograph of a place you have never been

hopeFeature.name: Witchwarper Hope Feature
hopeFeature.rules: Spend 3 Hope to have a spell affect all targets in your Quantum Field.

features.name: Quantum Field
features.rules: You have a Quantum Field. You can summon or dismiss it at the start of your spotlight. Summon it at a point within Far range by marking 1 Stress. It is destroyed if it exceeds Far range from you. Everywhere within Very Close range of the center of your Quantum Field is considered "Within your Field". You can only select Spell domain cards. With every spell, replace "within Melee/Very Close/Close/Far/Very Far" with the phrase "within your Field". Spell effects occur only within your Field. Describe summoned creatures and fiends as entities from other dimensions, and necrotic energy as entropic.

features.name: Wave Function
features.rules: At the start of your spotlight you may move the center of your Quantum Field to any point currently within it. During your spotlight you can forgo your own movement to move your Quantum Field to a new point currently within it, and may mark a Stress to do so again.

backgroundQuestions: What did you notice in the cracks of the world that made you realize it was not as solid as everyone said?
Which version of your life do you sometimes glimpse, and who is in it that is not here now?
Who first noticed you slipping between moments, and how did they explain it away?
connections: I remember something you say never happened. What was it, and why are you so sure I'm wrong?
I once bent the world a little to help you out of a jam, and something small came back different. What changed?
What is the one thing about you that stays the same in every version of you I have glimpsed?

classes.name: Mechanic
classes.classItems: A multitool worn to the shape of your hand or a mismatched bolt you keep because you cannot remember what it came from

hopeFeature.name: Mechanic Hope Feature
hopeFeature.rules: Spend 3 Hope to recreate your Sidekick. Alternately, you can Prepare during a long rest and forgo gaining Hope to summon your Sidekick.

features.name: Trusty Sidekick
features.rules: You have an invention of circuits and parts, small enough to be carried as a backpack, that accompanies you. It has 4 Armor Slots plus 1 per Tier, has Evasion equal to yours, and moves with you to stay in Very Close range of you. It can be equipped with any secondary weapon, giving you that weapon's benefits as though you had it equipped. When its final Armor Slot is marked, it is destroyed.

features.name: Machine Whisperer
features.rules: Your Sage domain cards apply to technological and urban systems instead of natural environments: tracking can work through computer systems, a familiar can be a small drone, and speaking with the natural world becomes conversing with turrets, ship AIs, and databases. Magic damage from these cards is instead Tech or physical damage, your choice.

backgroundQuestions: Which wreck, workshop, or scrapyard first taught you that everything broken is just waiting to be understood?
You built something you were proud of, and someone borrowed it and never gave it back. What was it, and who has it?
Who trusted you with their ship, their gear, or their only way home before you really knew what you were doing, and how did it go?
connections: You once brought me a machine that would not work, and I fixed it without asking where you found it. What was it?
I built or repaired something just for you. What is it, and what does it do that you never asked for?
What sound from my gear or tools tells you I am worried?

classes.name: Technomancer
classes.classItems: A cracked data slate that boots to a single locked file or a worn charm made of old circuit boards

hopeFeature.name: Technomancer Hope Feature
hopeFeature.rules: Mark 1 Armor Slot to gain 2 Hope, or spend 2 Hope to clear 1 Armor Slot.

features.name: Machine Whisperer
features.rules: Your Sage domain cards apply to technological and urban systems instead of natural environments: tracking can work through computer systems, a familiar can be a small drone, and speaking with the natural world becomes conversing with turrets, ship AIs, and databases. Magic damage from these cards is instead Tech or physical damage, your choice. On Codex domain cards, replace "Book" and "Grimoire" with "Program".

features.name: Versatile Caster
features.rules: Mark a Stress or spend a Hope to alter the damage type and/or flavor of any spell. Damage types include magic, Tech, and physical. Flavor never changes damage dice, ranges, or durations.

backgroundQuestions: What system, network, or forgotten archive first answered you when it should have been silent?
Who taught you to treat code as something that listens, and what did it ask of you in return?
You once opened something you were told to leave alone. What was inside, and who knows you did it?
connections: I trusted you with a secret I had stored where no one else could reach. What was it, and how did you keep it safe?
I taught you one trick that makes technology bend a little for you. What was it, and what did I ask for in return?
We once stood in front of a machine neither of us understood. What did it do, and what did we decide?

classes.name: Biohacker
classes.classItems: A vial of your own blood, labeled in an old and shaky hand or a seed pod from a plant that should not grow on this world

hopeFeature.name: Biohacker Hope Feature
hopeFeature.rules: Spend 3 Hope to refill your Serum Pool.

features.name: Serum Pool
features.rules: You have a pool of Serum Tokens that can hold tokens equal to your Tier plus your Spellcast Trait. Once per spotlight you can deliver a dose of serum by succeeding on a weapon attack or a Spellcast Roll (Difficulty 14) and then spending a Serum Token. Some creatures (at the GM's discretion) may make a reaction roll to negate it, against a Difficulty equal to the result of your action roll.

features.name: Tech Caster
features.rules: Any magic damage is instead Tech damage.

features.name: Minor Serums
features.rules:
When you deliver a dose of serum, pick one of the following temporary effects to apply to a single one of your targets. Lingering effects last the rest of this scene or until the GM spends a Fear to end them. Only the most recent serum per target applies.
- The target clears or marks a Stress.
- The target's Difficulty or Evasion is modified by +2/-2 (lingering).
- A PC's trait is improved by +1 (lingering).

backgroundQuestions: Which lab, clinic, or wild habitat first showed you that life can be rewritten, and what did it cost you to learn?
You once experimented on yourself and the results stuck. What changed, and who understood why you did it?
Who did you patch up with a treatment you were not supposed to use yet, and how are they doing now?
connections: You came to me sick, hurt, or changed. What did I do, and what did I ask you to keep quiet?
I took a sample from you once, with your permission. What did I learn that surprised us both?
What habit of mine tells you right away that I have not been looking after myself?

classes.name: Aspis Sleeper
classes.classItems: A blank identity chip worn thin by many names or a child's toy that you cannot explain keeping

hopeFeature.name: Aspis Sleeper Hope Feature
hopeFeature.rules: Spend 3 Hope to increase your Buried Protocols bonus by +2 for the rest of the scene and immediately use it on an action roll.

features.name: Force of Will
features.rules: When you succeed with Fear on a Grace domain ability against one or more targets, a target of your choice you succeeded against marks a Stress.

features.name: Buried Protocols
features.rules: You gain a new Experience at +1 called "Buried Protocols". It increases by +1 each time you increase your Tier, and can be increased via leveling options as well, to a maximum of +7. Once per rest when you succeed on a roll while using it you can clear a Stress and gain a Hope.

backgroundQuestions: Who placed you in a quiet life, and what were you told to wait for?
You were told to watch someone and report on them, and you left things out. Who were they, and who knows?
What name did you grow into that you wish you could keep, and who called you by it?
connections: You saw something about me that I was meant to keep hidden. What was it, and what did we agree to say about it?
I told you what I was meant to do before I met this crew. What did you say, and what do we do about it now?
I gave you a signal that means I need help but cannot ask. What is it?

features.name: Get 'Em
features.rules: You can initiate a number of Tag Team Rolls per session equal to your Tier. You can spend Envoy Tokens in place of Hope for this, one for one.

features.name: Stay on Target
features.rules: Once per session you can increase the value of another player's Hope Die or Fear Die by 1.

features.name: You've Got This
features.rules: When another player rolls with Fear, spend an Envoy Token to let them clear 1d4 Stress.

features.name: Focus Fire
features.rules: Once per scene, spend a Hope or an Envoy Token to designate an adversary for the rest of the scene. Allies add +1d6 to their attack rolls against that adversary.

features.name: In Plain Sight
features.rules: Each scene, until you attack that scene, you may use your Presence instead of Finesse to hide and need only props or a small crowd to hide in.

features.name: Lie Detector
features.rules: Spend an Envoy Token to ask the GM about a specific NPC statement this scene. They must tell you which parts are true and which are lies, but not the extent or contents of any lie.

features.name: Every Last Drop
features.rules: With a quick conversation you may spend an Envoy Token and an ally may mark a Stress to refresh one of their once per rest or once per long rest features.

features.name: Contingencies
features.rules: While you have 2 or more Envoy Tokens, you have a new death move: "Contingencies: Spend all Envoy Tokens and all Hope. Describe how an adversary in this scene dies instead, exactly as you planned from the start. Then follow the instructions of the Avoid Death move."

features.name: Arcane Font
features.rules: When you cast a spell, gain a VP. Spend 3 VP before you cast a spell to gain one of the following effects on a success: (A) increase a die size listed in the spell by 1 (a d20 becomes d20+6), (B) increase the range by 1 range band, or (C) cast it as though standing at the location of another creature in your Mystic Bond.

features.name: Crimson Rite
features.rules: Spend 2 VP after a successful Spellcast Roll to increase the Proficiency of this attack by 1.

features.name: Wellspring
features.rules: When you critically succeed on a Spellcast Roll, refill your VP.

features.name: Weaver
features.rules: During your spotlight you may choose up to 3 different effects from Arcane Font and Crimson Rite to apply to a spell, paying the VP for each.

features.name: Full Hearts
features.rules: You refill your VP each rest instead of each long rest. When you would gain a Hope, you may gain a VP instead. If your action roll was with Hope, clearing an ally's Stress or Hit Point costs 1 VP instead of 2.

features.name: Empathic Bond
features.rules: When an ally within your Mystic Bond clears more than 1 Hit Point or more than 1 Stress, gain a VP.

features.name: Constant Gardener
features.rules: You can use your Vitality Network twice per spotlight instead of once.

features.name: Shared Trauma
features.rules: When an ally within your Mystic Bond would mark a Hit Point, you may mark a Stress and spend 2 VP to reduce the damage by one threshold.

features.name: Sacrificial Act
features.rules: When an ally within your Mystic Bond would make a death move, you may switch places with them as a reaction. You make a death move instead, which cannot be Avoid Death. They receive the benefits of a long rest immediately and take the spotlight next. This can't be interrupted by spending Fear.

features.name: Precision 1
features.rules: When you add an Experience to a Called Shot, increase the extra damage to d6 instead of d4.

features.name: Pride in Your Work
features.rules: If you roll a Called Shot with Hope, gain an additional Hope.

features.name: Precision 2
features.rules: Your Called Shot bonus damage is always a d6, and now increases to a d8 if you added an Experience to it.

features.name: Run and Gun
features.rules: You can move before, but not after, your Called Shot.

features.name: Baba Yaga
features.rules: Your Operative Hope Feature now costs 1 Hope.

features.name: Collector
features.rules: When you make a Tech Roll (or a weapon roll that deals Tech damage) with Hope, put a token on this card, up to 6. Each rest, declare Gadget or Ordnance (see Starheart Consumables) and then spend all tokens to roll a d20 for each. Keep a number of results equal to your Knowledge Trait. Only you can use these inventions, and they become junk at the start of your next rest.

features.name: Tinker
features.rules: When rolling for your Collector feature, you may roll 1d12 + any number from 1 through 10 instead of 1d20.

features.name: Extra Juice
features.rules: Mark a Stress. For the rest of the scene, when you deal Tech damage to an adversary, they also mark 1 Stress.

features.name: Recycler
features.rules: When you use a Gadget, you may mark 2 Stress to prevent it from being consumed. At the start of your rest, prevent one Gadget or Ordnance from falling apart.

features.name: Shareable
features.rules: You can freely share your inventions, up to one per ally at a time. Sharing more causes previous inventions to fall apart.

features.name: Warpage
features.rules: When you attack with Hope, your Mote can (Photon) push or (Graviton) pull the target it strikes up to Very Close range.

features.name: Slingshot
features.rules: You may destroy your Weapon to make an Instinct Roll instead of an Agility Roll to move. With Graviton, you have advantage. With Photon, deal Pd6 damage to targets in Melee range before you move.

features.name: Lensing
features.rules: While your Aura is in place, increase your Evasion by 2.

features.name: Alignment
features.rules: When you attack an adversary directly between you and an ally, either (Photon) you have advantage on the attack roll, or (Graviton) the target has disadvantage on attacks against either of you.

features.name: Retrograde
features.rules: When an adversary attacks you, but before damage is rolled, you can destroy all your conjurations to shift into Very Close range, causing the attack to miss.

features.name: Well
features.rules: When a creature moves toward you, you may mark a Stress to either (Graviton) allow them double movement with no roll required, or (Photon) make a Spellcast Roll as a reaction to stop them halfway.

features.name: Expulse
features.rules: On a mode switch, a target adversary in Melee range makes a reaction roll (Difficulty 12 + your Spellcast Trait). On a failure, they (Photon) mark 1 Hit Point or (Graviton) mark 1 Stress.

features.name: Stellar Hunger
features.rules: On a critical hit with your Weapon or Mote, gain 2 Hope instead of 1 and clear 2 Stress instead of 1.

features.name: Gleaming Blade
features.rules: Increase your Solar Weapon damage by 1 die size and add +2 (d10+2 and d12+4).

features.name: Radiant Aura
features.rules: Once per rest, destroy your Aura to make a Spellcast Roll against all targets in Close range. Deal Pd4+6 Tech damage to each target you succeed against. Deal 1 damage to all others.

features.name: Supernova
features.rules: Spend 2 Hope. Make a Spellcast Roll. Graviton: Targets within Far range you succeed against are pulled into Very Close range of you, mark 1 Hit Point and 2 Stress, and are temporarily Restrained. Photon: Targets within Very Close range you succeed against are pushed to Far range, mark 2 Hit Points and 1 Stress, and are temporarily Vulnerable.

features.name: Overwhelm
features.rules: You do not need to spend a Hope to apply Suppressed.

features.name: Primary Target
features.rules: Once per rest you can declare a Primary Target. Gain a Hope any time your Primary Target marks a Hit Point. When your Primary Target succeeds on a reaction roll, you may mark a Stress to make them reroll and take the new result.

features.name: Quick Swap
features.rules: You do not need to mark a Stress when you switch weapons on your spotlight, but are still limited to one switch per spotlight.

features.name: Relentless Pursuit
features.rules: While your Primary Target is Suppressed, movement does not end their Suppressed condition and your attacks against them have advantage.

features.name: Terrifying Barrage
features.rules: When you apply Suppressed, you may spend a Hope to apply it to each other target in Very Close range of the first, spending a Hope for each.

features.name: Armor Master
features.rules: Your Hope Feature works while you have more than 2 Hope instead of more than 4. You may ignore any feature of armor you are wearing. Whenever you would make a Presence roll, you may make a Strength roll instead.

features.name: Quick Stitch
features.rules: When you clear any Armor Slots during a rest, clear that many Armor Slots, distributed as you like, among your allies as well.

features.name: Aegis Protocol
features.rules: If you spend Hope instead of marking an Armor Slot, you may then also mark an Armor Slot to further reduce your damage.

features.name: Heavyweight
features.rules: While using a Strength or Presence weapon, add your Armor Score to your damage.

features.name: That's Impossible
features.rules: When you would take damage and have 2 or more Hope, spend all Hope to reduce the damage to 0 and negate any effect the attack would have applied.

features.name: Ties that Bind
features.rules: Gain access to the Splendor domain. Choose one additional domain card from it.

features.name: Soothing Pulse
features.rules: When any target starts their spotlight within your Field, you may have them clear a Stress.

features.name: Expansion
features.rules: Increase the size of your Quantum Field to encompass all points within Close range, instead of Very Close. You can no longer mark a Stress to move it twice during your spotlight.

features.name: Strong Force
features.rules: When a creature moves more than Very Close range on its spotlight and enters your Field, you may elect to stop its movement. When a creature starts its spotlight within your Field, you may elect to reduce its movement distances by half.

features.name: Slowed Strikes
features.rules: As a reaction you can reduce any physical damage that passes through your Field by 1 die, or by half if no dice were used.

features.name: Quantum Tunneling
features.rules: Mark 2 Stress to open a wormhole to a point within your Field. Creatures and objects passing through emerge on the other side retaining their facing, and onlookers can see through the Field in the same direction they are looking. The tunnel closes at the end of your next spotlight.

features.name: Destructive Nature
features.rules: Gain access to the Arcana domain. Choose one additional domain card from it.

features.name: Violent Frequencies
features.rules: At the start of your spotlight, one target within your Field marks a Hit Point if they fail a reaction roll (Difficulty 14).

features.name: Probability Cloud
features.rules: Mark a Stress as a reaction after any action roll you see to add or subtract your Spellcast Trait to the result. This doesn't create or remove critical effects.

features.name: Swift Effect
features.rules: When you forgo movement to move your Quantum Field, move it to anywhere within Far range of its current position.

features.name: Phenomenal Effect
features.rules: You can have up to 6 cards in your loadout.

features.name: Abrupt Appearance
features.rules: When you summon your Quantum Field, all targets you elect within it, including other player characters, must mark 1 Hit Point.

features.name: Armor Up
features.rules: Your Sidekick can manifest as a mech suit for you. When summoned this way, the Sidekick has no Armor Slots of its own; instead clear a number of your Armor Slots equal to what it would have had. It uses your damage thresholds. You still gain the benefits of its equipped secondary weapon. Choose one primary weapon you have in your inventory each time you summon your Sidekick. That weapon now uses your Spellcast Trait when making attacks.

features.name: Working as Intended
features.rules: You can mark a Stress to mark an additional Armor Slot when you take damage. Whenever you mark more than 1 Armor Slot at a time, gain 1 Hope.

features.name: One with the Machine
features.rules: Your Sidekick is no longer destroyed unless you allow it. Whenever your armor is fully marked, you can spend all Hope to clear that many Armor Slots.

features.name: Configurable
features.rules: When you summon your Sidekick, and at each long rest, choose one of the following features: flying; submersible; resistant to one damage type of your choice; advantage on Spellcast Rolls; advantage on attack rolls. Your Sidekick loses the last property it had and gains this one.

features.name: Transformer
features.rules: When you summon your Sidekick, choose one of the following features for it: Hovering; +2 Armor Score; +2 Evasion. Its thresholds by Tier are 7/15, 11/24, 13/31, 15/40. Describe its form when you create it.

features.name: Telecast
features.rules: When you cast a spell you can use your Sidekick as the origin point for it. When you take the spotlight, you can elect to act solely through your Sidekick or on your own. If you start your spotlight in Very Close range of it, you can have it follow your movements.

features.name: More than Meets the Eye
features.rules: When you summon your Sidekick, choose one of the following features for it: a secret compartment shielded from Tech, magic, and physical sensors and forces; advantage on movement action rolls; advantage on reaction rolls.

features.name: Follow-up
features.rules: When your Sidekick succeeds with Hope against a target you could attack without moving, you can attack that target as a reaction.

features.name: Robot in Disguise
features.rules: Mark a Stress to render your Sidekick invisible or disguised from casual observation. If any target scans it, make a Knowledge reaction roll to prevent being detected.

features.name: Master of Your Craft
features.rules: You can resummon your Sidekick for 2 Hope instead of 3 Hope.

features.name: Always Working
features.rules: Each rest, in addition to your rest actions, you may roll a d20 on either the Cypher or Gadget consumables page and gain that object. You can hold up to 4 such objects at any time.

features.name: Improvised Magic
features.rules: When you cast a spell you can spend a Cypher or Gadget to pay any cost associated with the spell.

features.name: Efficiency
features.rules: When you use Always Working, roll 3d20 on one table and 1d20 on the other. Keep any 3 of the 4 results.

features.name: Storage Improvement
features.rules: You can hold up to 6 such objects instead of 4.

features.name: The Right Tool
features.rules: Sacrifice a Cypher or Gadget to gain advantage on a Spellcast Roll.

features.name: Magical Battery
features.rules: When you or an ally casts a spell, place a token on this card. You can hold a maximum of 6. When an ally in Close range makes an action or reaction roll, spend tokens for a +1 bonus each on the result of their roll. You can do so after the roll but before consequences have been announced.

features.name: Capacitance
features.rules: If you have no Magical Battery tokens left, the first time you would gain a token, gain 2 instead. Increase your maximum token count to 8.

features.name: Shielding
features.rules: Spend tokens to add +1 per token to both thresholds of an ally in Close range. This new threshold lasts the rest of the scene, or until you use this effect again.

features.name: Defrag
features.rules: When you cast a spell, you can swap it for another spell card in your vault, paying 1 less Stress than the swap normally costs.

features.name: Overclock
features.rules: When you use your Versatile Caster class feature, you may also (A) extend the range by one range band, (B) reduce the cost by 1 Stress or Hope, or (C) increase the damage die along this track: d4 -> d6 -> d8 -> d10 -> d12 -> d12+d4 -> d20 -> d20+d6.

features.name: Mutative Effect
features.rules: Each long rest you can splice the genes of a willing ally. Give them a copy of any Bone domain card in your vault or loadout. It counts as a transformation for them, and is removed at their next long rest.

features.name: Self Help
features.rules: Improve any one trait each long rest by +1. The trait you choose must be different from your most recently improved trait, and applying it removes the previous improvement.

features.name: Creature Feature
features.rules: Gain a new Experience: "Form of _______ +3". When you succeed on a weapon attack against an adversary, or when you examine their corpse, spend a Serum Token to take a sample of it. Replace the blank with the name of the sampled creature, and use it when their form would help you.

features.name: I Love My Work
features.rules: Taking a sample with Creature Feature costs no Serum Token. When you make an action roll with Hope, you can gain 2 Serum Tokens instead of 1 Hope.

features.name: Cataloger
features.rules: You have a log of creatures you've sampled with a number of slots equal to your Tier + your Knowledge. You can replace any name with any new sample you take. Mark a Stress to update your "Form of _______" Experience to a name on your list.

features.name: Intermediate Serums
features.rules:
Add to your list of serum effects the following:
- The target's reaction rolls have advantage/disadvantage.
- The target sees in the dark.
- The target changes color.
- The target gains a Hope.
- The target marks 1 Hit Point (costs 2 Serum Tokens).

features.name: Chemical Cocktail
features.rules: You can spend 2 Serum Tokens to affect the same target twice. Your Minor Serum effects can stack.

features.name: Ample Ampules
features.rules: If you start a scene with fewer than 2 Serum Tokens, refill to 2 Serum Tokens.

features.name: Extra Strength
features.rules: Serum effects last until your next long rest.

features.name: Aerosol Dispersal
features.rules: Spend 3 Serum Tokens to impact all creatures in Very Close range with an effect of your choice.

features.name: Master Serums
features.rules:
Add to your list of serum effects the following:
- The target falls asleep.
- The target has disadvantage on action rolls.
- The target is rendered unable to sense other creatures, and other creatures are hidden from it.
- The target marks 1 Hit Point, and then you clear 1 Stress.

features.name: Undercover
features.rules: The first time each scene you succeed on a Finesse action roll, the GM loses 1 Fear if they have more than 3 Fear.

features.name: Who, Me?
features.rules: When a single adversary would sense you while you are Hidden, you can mark a Stress to make a Spellcast Roll as a reaction against them. On a success they seem to forget what they saw or heard.

features.name: Quickdraw
features.rules: You can hide any one-handed weapon on your person. If the weapon is hidden at the start of your spotlight, your first attack roll with it has advantage.

features.name: Escape Route
features.rules: Spend a Hope to unlock a mundane lock, loosen a panel, slip by a single guard, or otherwise facilitate a simple step in an infiltration plan.

features.name: Backstory
features.rules: When you succeed on a Presence roll or a non-attack Spellcast Roll against an NPC you can spend a Hope to have them accidentally give you a perfect backstory explaining your presence here.

features.name: Desperation
features.rules: Gain a new Experience called "Desperation". It has a bonus equal to your marked Hit Points.

features.name: Brutal Assault
features.rules: When you damage a target you can mark a Stress to force them to mark 1 more Hit Point.

features.name: Contract
features.rules: When you use your Buried Protocols Experience for an attack roll, add its bonus to your damage.

features.name: Take Down
features.rules: Before rolling an attack you can spend a Hope to declare a Take Down. If your attack then deals Severe damage, the target is taken out of the fight. The GM can spend 2 Fear to keep them in the fight at 1 Hit Point.

features.name: Fast Learner
features.rules: When an adversary succeeds on an attack against you, you can designate it as your Studied Adversary. When your Studied Adversary subsequently attacks you, reduce the damage you take by 1 threshold, to a minimum of 1.

features.name: Collateral
features.rules: Once per scene, if your attack defeats an adversary, you can roll your standard damage of that attack against another adversary in range.

items.name: Stride Stim
items.rules: You gain a +1 bonus to your next Agility Roll.

items.name: Bolster Stim
items.rules: You gain a +1 bonus to your next Strength Roll.

items.name: Control Stim
items.rules: You gain a +1 bonus to your next Finesse Roll.

items.name: Attune Stim
items.rules: You gain a +1 bonus to your next Instinct Roll.

items.name: Charm Stim
items.rules: You gain a +1 bonus to your next Presence Roll.

items.name: Enlighten Stim
items.rules: You gain a +1 bonus to your next Knowledge Roll.

items.name: Minor Health Stim
items.rules: Clear 1d4 HP.

items.name: Minor Stamina Stim
items.rules: Clear 1d4 Stress.

items.name: Morale Tabs
items.rules: Take this paired dose to immediately gain 2 Hope.

items.name: Sprite Bottle
items.rules: When you mark your last Hit Point, this bottle shatters to release the Sprite inside. The Sprite clears all your Hit Points before fading from the Mortal Realm.

items.name: Displacement Token
items.rules: You can swallow this token to conjure two illusions of yourself that you can control. Each illusion lasts until it takes damage or until your next rest.

items.name: Stonemason’s Fortune
items.rules: When you throw this gray brick on the ground, it immediately grows into a 6-foot-tall, 10-foot-wide, and 2-foot- deep wall of solid stone.

items.name: Homet’s Secret Potion
items.rules: After drinking this potion, the next successful attack you make critically succeeds.

items.name: Midas Flask
items.rules: You can pour this small flask of alchemical liquid over a mundane item to instantly transmute it into a handful of gold.

items.name: Staff of Reversal
items.rules: You can break this staff against the ground to reverse one magical transformation or effect within Far range.

items.name: Berserker’s Brew
items.rules: When you drink this dram of liquid, you gain a bonus to your Strength and a penalty to your Finesse and Knowledge equal to your Instinct (minimum 1). This effect lasts until you make a death move or until your next rest.

items.name: Hopehold Flare
items.rules: When you use this flare, allies within Close range roll a d6 when they spend a Hope. On a result of 6, they gain the effect of that Hope without spending it. The flare lasts until the end of the scene.

items.name: Circle of the Void
items.rules: Mark a Stress to create a void that extends up to Far range. No magic can be cast inside the void, and creatures within the void are immune to magic damage.

items.name: Cacophonous Concoction
items.rules: When you drink this potion, anything you say or do in the next hour becomes impossible for a witness to recount. Any attempts they make to communicate what they saw, heard, or otherwise sensed comes out garbled or nonsensical.

items.name: Nightmare Mead
items.rules: You can drink this potion to discover the deepest fear of the next person you make eye contact with. When you do, the GM gains a Fear.

items.name: Stake of Abjuration
items.rules: You can hammer this stake into the ground and make a proclamation. Until your next rest, a creature within Far range of the stake who transgresses that proclamation must mark a Stress. The stake lasts until your next rest, then it shatters.

items.name: Psychopomp’s Shroud
items.rules: You can place this shroud over the corpse of a recently deceased creature. The creature’s spirit enters the shroud and becomes your spectral assistant until the next sunrise, when they pass through the veil of death and take the shroud with them.

items.name: Phial of Deep Ink
items.rules: You can drink this bottle of ink to transform into a cephalopod of roughly your size for the next hour. You gain rubbery skin, soft bones, the ability to breathe underwater, and new limbs until you have eight total.

items.name: Mesmer’s Tonic
items.rules: When you drink this tonic, the only thing you can hear until your next rest are the surface thoughts of creatures within Very Close range.

items.name: Formoid Serum
items.rules: You can drink this potion to become a swarm of 16 million ants until the end of the scene. You keep and have access to all equipment, loot, and features.

items.name: Steelskin Salve
items.rules: You can apply this salve to your skin to gain a bonus to your damage thresholds equal to your tier until the end of the scene.

items.name: Block House
items.rules: Toss this wooden block to conjur a phatasmal doorway where it lands. Within occupants can close and seal the door, erasing it from the world. At the end of 1 day everything brought in appears at the threshold and the door vanishes forever.

items.name: Snakeskin Spirit
items.rules: You can drink this potion to slough off your outer layer of skin and heal a scar.

items.name: Bonding Honey
items.rules: This honey can be used to glue two objects together permanently.

items.name: Magic-User’s Malison
items.rules: When you release this spellcaster’s trapped soul, you can cast one spell from a card in your vault as if it were in your loadout. This doesn’t work for permanently vaulted cards.

items.name: Shrinking Potion
items.rules: You can drink this potion to halve your size until you choose to drop this form or your next rest. While in this form, you have a +2 bonus to Agility and a −1 penalty to your Proficiency.

items.name: Quintessential Severant
items.rules: You can use this magic blade to cut one magical or metaphysical bond, such as an enchantment, contract, magical tether, or divine oath. When you do, the blade shatters.

items.name: Growing Potion
items.rules: You can drink this potion to double your size until you choose to drop this form or your next rest. While in this form, you have a +2 bonus to Strength and a +1 bonus to your Proficiency.

items.name: Mask of the Echoed Self
items.rules: You can wear this mask during your next level up to swap the values of any of your traits. When you do, the mask becomes your permanent face.

items.name: Knowledge Stone
items.rules: If you die while holding this stone, an ally can take a card from your loadout to place in their loadout or vault. After they take this knowledge, the stone crumbles.

items.name: Necroprancer’s Bell
items.rules: You can break this rusted, clapperless bell against the ground to summon a skeletal steed that climbs out of the earth and serves you until the next sunrise.

items.name: Drakemantle
items.rules: You can use this enchanted ancient dragon hide to gain draconic characteristics until the end of the scene, when the hide falls aways in tatters. Until then, you can fly and gain a +5 bonus to your damage thresholds and a +1 bonus to your Proficiency.

items.name: Lionheart Tonic
items.rules: You can drink this tonic to gain a +1 bonus to your Proficiency until you roll with Fear.

items.name: Tears of the Undying Hero
items.rules: When you drink this potion, death can’t touch you until your next long rest. When you would mark your last Hit Point, instead of making a death move, you make one final action roll before falling into a dreamless slumber until an ally chooses the Tend to Wounds downtime move to clear your Hit Points.

items.name: Steward Aegis Beacon
items.rules: Light to fill an area within Close range with a protective field. A creature outside it can't enter if it has ill intent toward a creature inside. Lasts an hour.

items.name: Castrovel Chameleon Spray
items.rules: Spray on yourself to blend perfectly into natural environments until your next rest.

items.name: Voxsplice Lozenge
items.rules: Dissolve to perfectly mimic any voice you've heard until the end of the scene.

items.name: Fall-Damp Ampoule
items.rules: Drink to ignore falling damage for 10 minutes.

items.name: Null-G Dust
items.rules: Anything this dust covers becomes weightless for an hour. One packet covers a small crate's contents.

items.name: Low-Light Ocular Drops
items.rules: Apply to see in total darkness until your next rest.

items.name: Pharasmin Echo Powder
items.rules: Sprinkle on a recently deceased corpse to project a holographic replay of their final minute of life.

items.name: Pharasmin Grave Salt
items.rules: Spread in a line along windowsills or thresholds. Undead creatures can't cross it until the line is broken.

items.name: Glowspore Pod
items.rules: Break apart to make it glow bright blue until your next long rest.

items.name: Morphic Gel
